notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Roadmap renumbered after splitting secure core from runtime secrets; now M5.

problem: AI coding agents currently obtain broad secret files even when they only need a narrow runtime capability.
rollback: Disable MCP runtime mutation tools and retain read-only status/audit operations if capability enforcement is not safe enough.
scope: Expose project/environment status, lifecycle, synchronization, audit and runtime operations through MCP over the same domain services used by CLI/Web.
Treat AI/agent sessions as principals when identity context is available.
Prefer scoped runtime/capability operations over returning raw secret plaintext.
Support access-request/approval semantics for sensitive scopes where the policy model requires human approval.
Ensure MCP operations create attributable audit events.
title: Milestone 5: MCP and AI-native runtime access
validation: An MCP client can inspect environment synchronization, drift and expiry state.
An authorized MCP client can start an approved development runtime without receiving a bulk plaintext .env payload.
MCP runtime and access actions are attributable to the initiating principal/session in audit.
Raw plaintext secret retrieval is not required for the primary MCP workflows.
value: Make secure credentials a native capability for coding agents rather than an unsafe file-sharing workaround.
